guidance.title: Guide
guidance.disclaimer: Typical figures for everyday driving. Your owner's manual is the final word for your car.

diy.easy: Easy: about 10 minutes with no tools, and you'll save most of the cost.
diy.moderate: Possible with basic tools and a safe way to lift the car. Most people use a shop.

oil_change.what: Draining old engine oil and replacing it and the oil filter.
oil_change.why: Oil keeps the engine's moving parts from grinding against each other. Old oil breaks down and lets wear build up, which leads to expensive engine damage.

tire_rotation.what: Moving each tire to a different position on the car.
tire_rotation.why: Front and rear tires wear differently. Rotating them evens out wear so the set lasts longer and the car grips evenly.

brake_inspection.what: Checking brake pads, rotors and lines for wear or damage.
brake_inspection.why: Catching thin pads early is cheap. Waiting until they grind can ruin the rotors and double the bill, and worn brakes stop the car later.

brake_fluid.what: Flushing out old brake fluid and replacing it.
brake_fluid.why: Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, which lowers its boiling point and corrodes parts. Old fluid can make the pedal feel soft when braking hard.

engine_air_filter.what: Replacing the filter that cleans air going into the engine.
engine_air_filter.why: A clogged filter makes the engine work harder and can lower fuel economy and power. Dusty and gravel roads clog it faster.

cabin_air_filter.what: Replacing the filter that cleans air coming through the vents.
cabin_air_filter.why: It traps dust, pollen and smoke. A clogged one makes the heat and A/C weaker and can cause musty smells and foggy windows.

coolant.what: Draining and replacing the engine or battery coolant.
coolant.why: Coolant keeps the engine from overheating in summer and freezing in winter. Old coolant loses its protection and can corrode the cooling system.

transmission_fluid.what: Replacing the fluid that lubricates and cools the transmission.
transmission_fluid.why: Worn fluid can cause rough or slipping shifts. A transmission is one of the most expensive parts to replace, so fresh fluid is cheap insurance.

spark_plugs.what: Replacing the plugs that ignite fuel in each cylinder.
spark_plugs.why: Worn plugs cause misfires, rough idling, harder cold starts and worse fuel economy.

battery_12v.what: Testing the small battery that powers starting, lights and electronics.
battery_12v.why: Cold weather is hard on batteries, and most fail without warning. A quick test before winter avoids a no-start on a freezing morning. EVs have one too.

hv_battery_check.what: A health check of the large battery that powers an EV or hybrid.
hv_battery_check.why: It shows how much capacity the battery has kept and catches cooling or cell problems early, while they may still be covered by warranty.

wiper_blades.why: Streaky wipers are a real safety issue in rain, snow and slush. Ice and road salt wear them out quickly in Canadian winters.
